notes: Yoruba pronouns (ó, wọ́n) are gender-neutral, so nothing agrees in gender with the player or a {name}; nothing is attached to a placeholder (no vowel elision such as sílé before a placeholder).
Plural has only other (Intl.PluralRules yo); counted nouns put the number after the noun (jagunjagun {n}).
Generated names are noun-first with a space (generatedNames: noun-first): Òkè + Àrá = Òkè Àrá, Ẹnubodè + Irin = Ẹnubodè Irin. First parts are nouns or modifiers that follow any noun, with no ti.
Yoruba letters ẹ ọ ṣ and combining tone marks are outside the bundled Latin-1 fonts: activating yo needs it in SYSTEM_FONT_LANGS (tests/locales/latin-fonts.test.ts fails until then).
The Japanese statutory pages are translated fully into Yoruba, as vi does; the support page links them by their Japanese titles.
ui.s_have_bced00a61e is the fragment the game puts into ui.your_purchase_been_delivered_6f88dee143 for several purchases; Yoruba uses àwọn (plural marker) placed before rírà in that sentence.
